common_name: Cascade Falls Bald Cypress (Weeping Groundcover-Form Bald Cypress)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped trees in spring in moist to wet, acidic to neutral soil in full sun; stake and train a leader early if a taller cascading specimen is wanted, since left alone it hugs the ground.

directions: Plant in consistently moist to occasionally wet, acidic to neutral soil in full sun, staking the central leader while young and tying it upward if a tall, cascading fountain form is the goal; left untrained, the branches sprawl outward and downward into a low, undulating mound. Cascade Falls is a strongly weeping selection of the native bald cypress, its soft, ferny, blue-green foliage draping in dense curtains that turn coppery rust before dropping for winter, making it a dramatic choice for spilling over a retaining wall, bank, or large container. Like the species it tolerates both swampy, seasonally flooded sites and ordinary well-drained garden soil, and develops the same distinctive rounded knees when grown in consistently wet ground. Prune out any vigorous upright shoots that revert toward the species' normal pyramidal habit to keep the weeping character intact.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Taxodium Cultivars
